notes.ente: Singular and plural: ente emwe, one cow; ente ibiri, two cows.
notes.zirya: Agrees with plural n- nouns: ente nizirya.
notes.pundamilia: Entuuro, zebra, common in Lake Mburo park.

guidebook.intro: Name animals on the farm and in the wild. Most animal words are n- nouns, which look the same in the singular and plural.

tips.title: One cow, many cows
body: **Ente** is one cow and also many cows. The other words in the sentence tell you which: **ente emwe** (one cow), **ente ibiri** (two cows), **ente nizirya** (the cows are eating).
Words for small or special things use **eki-/ebi-**: **ekinyonyi, ebinyonyi** (bird, birds); **ekisoro, ebisoro** (animal, animals).

culture.title: The Ankole cow
body: The long-horned Ankole cow, **ente y’Ankole**, is the region’s pride. Cows are counted as wealth, given at weddings and praised in poems called **ebyevugo**. Lake Mburo National Park is home to zebras, impala and hippos nearby.
